record.paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Find a closed-form generalized supernomial T(L,M,k,k') for n>=3 that realizes the unifying A_{n-1} identity suggested by the three conjectures in Section 7. The function should satisfy the limiting conditions that recover T((M1,M2),k)(q)_{M1+M2}, the reciprocal supernomial T'(L,k), and the cylindric-partition product T''(L1,M1,k,k'), and it should obey the reciprocal-q constraint T(L,M,k,k';1/q)/T(L,M,k,k';q)=q^(-M C L + sum_i k_i k'_i). The goal is an explicit closed form for T that makes the unifying signed sum identity valid when n>=3.

evidence.quote: strongly suggest the existence of a unifying identity
we have not succeeded in finding a closed form expression when n >= 3

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $n\ge 3$, construct an explicit closed-form "generalized supernomial" $T(L,M,k,k';q)$, depending on tuples of nonnegative integer parameters $L=(L_1,\ldots)$, $M=(M_1,\ldots)$ and integer vectors $k,k'$ indexed by the simple roots of $A_{n-1}$, with the following properties.

(a) (Cylindric/product limit) In an appropriate limit, $T$ reduces to the cylindric-partition product expression $T''(L_1,M_1,k,k';q)$ for $A_{n-1}$.

(b) (Reciprocal-supernomial limit) In another limit, $T$ reduces to the reciprocal supernomial $T'(L,k;q)$.

(c) ($A_1$ specialization) For $n=2$, $T$ reduces to $T((M_1,M_2),k;q)/(q)_{M_1+M_2}$, recovering the known $A_1$ generalized supernomial.

(d) (Reciprocal-$q$ symmetry) $T$ satisfies
$$\frac{T(L,M,k,k';1/q)}{T(L,M,k,k';q)} = q^{-\,M\,C\,L \;+\; \sum_i k_i k'_i},$$
where $C$ is the Cartan matrix of $A_{n-1}$.

Using such a $T$, establish the corresponding unifying signed-sum Rogers–Ramanujan-type identity at rank $A_{n-1}$ ($n\ge 3$) that simultaneously generalizes the three known conjectural identities recovered in limits (a)–(c).
artifact.status_search_result: A closed form for the unifying $A_{n-1}$ generalized supernomial with $n\ge 3$ does not appear in the literature. Surveys and follow-up works on supernomial coefficients and $A_{n-1}$ Bailey lemma (Schilling–Warnaar; Warnaar) continue to list higher-rank ($A_{n-1}$, $n\ge 3$) extensions and supernomial inversion as unsolved problems, with no published closed-form construction found.

status_evidence.title: SUPERNOMIAL COEFFICIENTS, BAILEY'S LEMMA AND ROGERS-RAMANUJAN-TYPE IDENTITIES
status_evidence.snippet: the intimately related, but unsolved problems of supernomial inversion, A_{n-1} and higher level extensions are also discussed
status_evidence.claim: Higher-rank A_{n-1} extensions of the supernomial framework are identified as unsolved problems.

status_evidence.title: Supernomial Coefficients, Polynomial Identities and q-Series
status_evidence.snippet: q-supernomial coefficients unify and extend boson-fermion identities for one-dimensional configuration sums
status_evidence.claim: The published supernomial framework treats A_1 in closed form but does not provide a general A_{n-1} closed form.
